idea.title: Calendly: personal scheduling links (as of 2013-06-01)

source.text: Calendly: scheduling links so people book a meeting without email back-and-forth, freemium with a paid plan at $8 per month, launch country US. Score it as of 2013-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a solo developer with $5,000 and full time. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug calendly.

idea.problem: Booking a meeting takes several emails of back-and-forth to find a time.
idea.solution: A personal scheduling link that shows open slots from the user's calendar so the other person books directly.
assumptions: Scored as of 2013-06-01 with evidence published on or before that date.
Target customer assumed: US independent professionals and salespeople who book many 1:1 meetings.
Goal assumed: a startup (full-time commitment), not side income.
Main channel assumed: the viral loop of the link itself (every invitee sees the product).
No existing audience, network or domain asset assumed (none stated).
Monthly churn assumed 4% (no dated prosumer benchmark found).

confidence.note: No dated 2013 pricing pages for ScheduleOnce/YouCanBook.me or a prosumer churn benchmark; those would firm up pricing_power and ltv_cac.

gross_margin.note: About 87% after Stripe 2.9%+30c (~$0.53) and ~$0.47 infra/email per payer (estimate).

ltv_cac.note: LTV $175 vs CAC ~$50 (estimate) = 3.5; viral link keeps CAC low, 4% churn caps LTV.

pricing_power.note: Free Doodle, Google slots and Atlas set a $0-5 anchor; Atlas plans Pro at $5/month.

build_effort.note: Google Calendar API v3 (2011) makes a link MVP a 1-2 month solo build.

skills_match.note: Solo developer: the core build is code; marketing and sales are the missing half.

capital_needed.note: Heroku/AWS at ~$50-100/month: $5,000 covers 12+ months of runway on infra.

time_to_mvp.note: About 8 weeks to a usable, reliable calendar sync plus billing (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve $8/month card payment via Stripe: same-day purchase, no procurement.

channel_readiness.note: Viral loop exists (98% of Doodle users came by invitation) but founder has no audience.

search_demand.note: Doodle had 10M monthly users, 2M in the US (2011): online scheduling is mass-market.

trend.note: Doodle US base grew ~4x in two years and still at 10M monthly users in 2012-07.

willingness_to_pay.note: SMBs pay $19.95-58/month for booking, but individuals expect free; freemium converts 0.5-4%.

free_alternatives.note: Doodle MeetMe (free) and Google appointment slots cover much of the job; not polished links.

competitor_density.note: 12+ tools: Doodle, TimeBridge, ScheduleOnce, Bookfresh, TimeTrade, Atlas, Meetin.gs.

differentiation.note: Tungle.me's shutdown (2012-12) left the signature-link use case open; edge is execution only.

legal_regulatory.note: Only CAN-SPAM; transactional booking emails are mostly exempt. No licence needed.

platform_dependency.note: Rides Google Calendar API; Google dropped deprecation guarantees and kills products.

market_risk.note: Meetings are a durable, daily need; scheduling is moving to mobile, not fading.

skills.note: Strong build skills; no stated go-to-market or sales track record.

assets.note: No audience, list, network or data stated.

interest.note: Motivation not stated; full-time commitment suggests more than curiosity.

tam.reasoning: 16.9M US independent workers (MBO 2012) x $96/year; upper bound, excludes salaried salespeople

sam.reasoning: 2M US Doodle users already scheduling online (TNW 2011) x $96/year

som.reasoning: 0.1% of SAM in year 1 = ~2,000 paying users x $96

competitors_found.reasoning: Named in dated sources: Doodle, MeetMe, BookMe, Google slots, Tungle (dead), TimeBridge, ScheduleOnce, Bookfresh, TimeTrade, Schedulicity, MyTime, Meetin.gs, Atlas, Groupon Scheduler

competitor_price_range.reasoning: Free (Doodle, Google slots, Atlas) to Bookfresh $19.95 and Doodle BookMe EUR 45 (~$58), 2012

price.reasoning: Founder's stated price; between free tools and $19.95+ SMB booking tools

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe 2.9% x $8 + $0.30 = $0.53, plus ~$0.47 hosting/email/support incl. free users carried per payer

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Above the 3% 'killer' threshold (Cummings 2012) because switching costs are low for an $8 prosumer tool

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Free-to-paid; Evernote 0.5% early to ~4% overall (2012); midpoint for a narrower tool

cac.reasoning: Organic/viral: ~1 founder hour per paying user at $50/h (outreach, launch posts, support); AdWords ruled out (Dropbox CPA $233-388)

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: ~8 weeks to MVP + 2 weeks for first free users to upgrade

verdict.launch_reason: Largest pool of independent workers and salespeople, and the home market of the free Google tools it must beat.
verdict.cheapest_test: A landing page plus a hand-run concierge link (Google appointment slots behind your domain) for 50 sales reps, with an $8/month pre-order button, 7 days.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 100 sign-ups from 500 targeted sales reps by day 7 -> stop or re-target
Fewer than 10 people say they would pay $8/month on the pricing step by day 7 -> drop the paid plan idea
Fewer than 20% of beta users send their link to 3+ invitees in week 1 -> the viral loop does not exist, stop

rescue.change: Sell to outbound salespeople and recruiters first: booking link in the email signature, team plan at $10/user/month.
rescue.why: Raises pricing_power, willingness_to_pay and differentiation: the Tungle signature use case has a buyer with a budget.
rescue.requires: Lists of sales reps on LinkedIn; team billing in Stripe

rescue.change: Capture Tungle.me refugees and list on the Google Apps Marketplace at launch.
rescue.why: Lifts channel_readiness: an orphaned user base plus a channel to 5M Google Apps businesses.
rescue.requires: Marketplace listing, migration page for Tungle users

rescue.change: Support Outlook/Exchange and iCal alongside Google Calendar from v1.
rescue.why: Cuts platform_dependency on a single Google API with no deprecation guarantee.

type_checks.note: Only 'over 3% monthly is killer' (2012) and enterprise-skewed Pacific Crest data; no dated prosumer benchmark. Modelled at 4%.
The incumbent is email back-and-forth; Tungle users moved to ScheduleOnce in weeks. Low switching costs help acquisition and hurt retention.

narrative.answer: **PIVOT, 68/100.** Demand is real and rising (Doodle: **10M monthly users**), costs are tiny and the link spreads itself. But free tools from Doodle and Google anchor the price near $0, and a solo $8 prosumer plan needs a paying niche first.
tldr: Demand is proven: Doodle had **10M monthly users** and 98% arrived by invitation, the same loop a booking link has.
The problem is price: **free** Doodle MeetMe, Google slots and Atlas set a $0-5 anchor for individuals.
Tungle.me's shutdown (2012-12) left the **signature-link** use case orphaned: start with salespeople who pay.

key_findings.title: Free tools anchor the price at zero
key_findings.detail: Doodle MeetMe (2011) and Google appointment slots (2011) give a **free** booking page; Atlas plans its Pro link at **$5/month** (2013-05).

key_findings.title: Demand is mass-market and viral
key_findings.detail: Doodle reached **10M monthly users**, 2M in the US, and **98%** found it through an invitation (TNW, 2011).

key_findings.title: The closest rival just died
key_findings.detail: RIM shut down Tungle.me on **2012-12-03**, orphaning salespeople who used a booking link in their **email signature**.

narrative.recommendation: Do not launch a generic $8 consumer plan. Launch for outbound salespeople and Tungle refugees, and pre-sell 10 paid seats in 7 days before building beyond an MVP.
narrative.steelman: A link that books meetings spreads itself with every invite, like Doodle's **98%** invitation-led growth, costs almost nothing to run, and Tungle's exit left the best use case unserved. The evidence supports demand and margin; it does not yet show that individuals pay.

premortem.cause: Users love the free tier but under 1% upgrade, because Doodle and Google already give the core job away.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2 upgrades per 100 active free users by day 30

premortem.cause: No differentiation from Atlas, Meetin.gs and Doodle MeetMe: launches get a spike, then flat sign-ups.
premortem.early_signal: Under 30% of new sign-ups come from invitee links after week 2

premortem.cause: A Google Calendar API change or a free Google feature undercuts the product.
premortem.early_signal: Google announces booking features or API quota cuts; over 5% of syncs fail in a week

why_now.note: APIs, payments and mobile all matured in 2011-2012, and Tungle's exit opened a gap; the free incumbents are the risk, not timing.

changes.what: Google Calendar API v3 launched with JSON and better recurring events.
Stripe launched publicly at 2.9% + 30c, making $8 self-serve billing trivial.
US smartphone ownership reached 46% of adults.
Google Apps passed 5M businesses on shared calendars.
Tungle.me, the leading booking-link tool, shut down.

icp.who: US outbound salespeople, recruiters and consultants booking 10+ external 1:1 meetings a week from Google Calendar
where: Hacker News and TechCrunch launch coverage
icp.pays_for_today: Mostly nothing (email, Doodle free); SMBs pay Bookfresh $19.95/month or Doodle BookMe EUR 45/month
icp.budget: unknown; sales tools are expensed per seat, likely $10-30/user/month
icp.trigger: Their scheduling tool shuts down (Tungle, 2012-12) or they start a high-volume outreach role

customer.segment: US salespeople, recruiters and independent professionals with many external 1:1 meetings
customer.pain: Several emails to agree a time; lost prospects when replies stall
customer.today: Email back-and-forth, Doodle polls, Google appointment slots, ScheduleOnce

use_cases.name: Sales rep booking demos from an email signature link
Consultant or coach booking client calls

free_alternative.evidence: Doodle MeetMe (2011-02) and Google Calendar appointment slots (2011-06) offer free booking pages; Atlas launched free in 2013-05.

strong_competitor.evidence: Doodle has 10M monthly users and a paid BookMe tier at EUR 45/month; TimeBridge had 500,000+ users; TimeTrade raised $5.6M.

graveyard.evidence: Tungle.me was acquired by RIM (2011-04) and shut down 2012-12-03; TimeBridge sold to MerchantCircle in 2010.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear: the link exposes every invitee, like Doodle's 98% invitation-led growth; Google Apps Marketplace reaches 2M+ businesses.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear: Stripe ~$0.53 per $8 charge and Heroku from $0.05/hour leave about 87% gross margin (estimate).

weak_demand.evidence: Clear: Doodle's US base grew about 4x in two years to 2M (2011) and held 10M monthly users in 2012.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Hit: Google removed deprecation guarantees for many APIs (2012-04) and closed 70 products by 2013-03; the product rides its Calendar API.

saturated_wave.evidence: Clear: about 5 look-alike launches in 12 months (Doodle BookMe, MyTime, Meetin.gs relaunch, Atlas, ScheduleOnce push), below 10.

risks.mitigation: Charge for team and sales features, not the link

risks.risk: Google Calendar API change or deprecation
Google ships a better free booking feature
Founder runs out of runway before traction (no salary in $5,000)

test_plan.step: Landing page: 'Put a booking link in your signature', $8/month pre-order button
Message 500 US sales reps and ex-Tungle users on LinkedIn and Twitter
Concierge: give 30 sign-ups a hand-set Google appointment-slot link on your domain
Ask each user to pre-pay $8 for month one
